Incorporating SLOOS signals into the FOMC assessment:

- Credit demand: Banks report stronger demand across C&I (large, middle-market, and small firms) and key consumer segments (credit cards, auto, and residential real estate). This points to resilient private-sector borrowing appetite, consistent with solid growth.
- Credit supply/standards: Banks indicate tighter consumer standards (higher minimum credit score requirements), and they expect higher delinquencies and charge-offs. CRE lending conditions remain cautious, aligning with broader stress in nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily, and construction segments.
- Policy read-through: Firming loan demand alongside “somewhat elevated” inflation and ongoing QT reduces urgency to ease policy, even as tighter standards and prospective credit quality deterioration argue for vigilance.

Net: The SLOOS tilt makes the communication slightly more hawkish than a pure “balanced risks” read, but ongoing credit caution and CRE vulnerabilities keep the tone only modestly so.
